scorecard.verdict: Tier 0 (honest). Hard gates ALL GREEN (G-T1..T5, incl. all-6-exact cut preservation on b8 and the temporal A/B flicker proof), stylizationStrength at ceiling 5.0, but identityConsistency 1.93 / motionFidelity 2.20 collapse on wide shots — the VLM: 'players are reduced to indistinct colored blobs' at 640x360 wide framing, exactly the ink-manga/cartoon-cel/anime failure class. The w5b structure-ADDITIVE thesis is PARTIALLY confirmed: identityConsistency 1.93 is the best of the flattened-family siblings (cartoon-cel 1.53, anime-npr 1.80, ink-manga 1.47) and criticalArtifacts 67 beats anime 136 / cartoon 99 / ink 88 — the facet field measurably helps identity vs the flatteners — but the improvement is nowhere near the frozen Tier-2 bar (every axis >= 4.0 + 0 critical + TL approval). Close-ups DO carry identity (ic=3-4 with jersey number/kit credited); the wide-shot 20-60px players still average into too few facets.

nextIncrement: measured precisely: identityConsistency 1.93 and motionFidelity 2.20 are the blockers (stylization 5.0 at ceiling; temporalConsistency 2.87 — the mesh reads as stable but residual vertex drift is visible). The gap is RESOLUTION x DENSITY: at 640x360 a 20-60px player is covered by ~3-8 facets of a 1500-anchor mesh. Attack paths, in measured order of promise: (a) subject-adaptive density — subject-toon's mask-gentle architecture applied to the mesh (player regions get 3-5x anchor density, background stays sparse; the saliency top-up already biases there but not enough), (b) the SLIC superpixel profile (600-1200 segments = ~2-4x the effective facet count on players, pip-class posture recorded), (c) neural keyframe path (the SPR104-class ControlNet/EbSynth accelerator). All three ride the same segment-label skeleton this trial shipped.
